Commonwealth Games live updates: Diamonds face their toughest match yet, swimming program wraps up
It's day six of the Commonwealth Games which means the Diamonds have perhaps their toughest match-up of the group stage against South Africa.
Over in the pool, the swimming wraps up with Lakeisha Patterson trying to equal her haul of three Paralympic gold medals with a third Commonwealth title in the women's 100m S9 freestyle.
Follow all the action in our live blog.

Wed 29 Jul 2026 at 6:45pm
About last night
There's a case to say that Australian athletics has never had it as good as it does now.
Last night, amidst the teeming rain of Glasgow, Lachie Kennedy and Torrie Lewis delivered spellbinding performances that simply sizzled.
Here's Jon Healy's view of the night from a sodden Scotstoun.
Wed 29 Jul 2026 at 6:37pm
Premature fist bumping left Peyton Craig 'pissed off for days'
Don't expect any early fist-bumps from Australia's Peyton Craig at the Commonwealth Games.
The 21-year-old middle-distance gun has learnt his lesson.
But he did it the hard way, after a premature celebration with Bob Abdelrahimat the national championships in April cost him a spot in the 800m semifinals.
As the pair went to make contact, a diving Degras Amekata pinched the second qualifying spot from Craig by four-hundreths of a second.
"At the time I was heated. I was pissed off for probably two days afterwards," Paris Olympian Craig recalled.
"Especially sitting from the sideline watching the national final knowing I could be competitive in it, but it's a lesson.
"I'm still only 21, I've got a lot of lessons to learn. I'll never do it again, that's for sure, and thankfully it didn't have too many repercussions on the rest of the season.
"Fist-bumps are put away for now. They're banned."
Craig opened his Commonwealth Games campaign in vastly different fashion with a much stronger finish at Scotstoun Stadium, surging home late to secure third in his 800m heat.
Craig admitted he was caught slightly off-guard when England's Max Burgin set a hot pace.
The Australian got stuck mid-pack but gritted his teeth and fought his way through, later describing the run as a "rust-buster".
"My coach Craig [Mottram] is very big on - while obviously we get out with intent - having the ability to relax and get yourself out of any situation," Craig said.
"I feel like that really helped me. I wasn't in a great spot through the bell and still not in a great spot with 200 to go.
"But it's just backing myself and backing the kick. I've always had a strong finish and I knew I just had enough to get it done, and thankfully I did."
AAP
Wed 29 Jul 2026 at 6:30pm
Weightlifting: Bella Andueza is up first
No time to waste this evening, as the women's 77kg weightlifting gets underway at the Armadillo.
Australia has Bella Andueza in this one, semifinalist at the CrossFit games, this is her Commonwealth Games debut.
Wed 29 Jul 2026 at 6:25pm
Hello everyone
Good day or good night to everyone reading and welcome to the ABC Sport coverage of the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
My name is Simon Smale and I, alongside James Tugwell, will be taking you through the first part of today's action from here in Australia, while Jon Healy will once more be out and about in the wilds of Glasgow.
As I made my way to the office today, a gorgeous golden moon was rising (thanks to the planned burns in Brisbane), and I figured it was a wonderful premonition about what to expect over the course of the next few hours as this typically successful golden Games continues for Australia.
In the first part of the day we have action in the pool, on the track, on the rink, on the platform and on the court.
Lots to get through, so get aboard the hype bus and join us - destination, the podium, probably.

Commonwealth Games: Australian swimmers add nine golds with dead-heat, Kai Taylor win and Shayna Jack tears
Australia's swimmers clinched a record medal tally in the pool, finishing the Commonwealth Games with an unprecedented 37 gold medals after an epic finale at Glasgow's swimming centre on day six.
Kyle Chalmers earned the 10th gold medal of his Commonwealth Games career, propelling him past Ian Thorpe's Australian men's record tally of 10 golds and one silver.
Chalmers, resigned to the end of his domestic 100m freestyle reign after his defeat by Flynn Southam 24 hours earlier, shared his glorious moment with compatriot Ben Armbruster as they both struck gold together in a Games record 22.73 seconds.
Chalmers responded as only the great champions can by also downing his fellow big gun Cam McEvoy, who took bronze in yet another Australian 1-2-3 in the pool.
The win gave Chalmers his 12th Games medal overall to rise above Thorpe.
"Maybe I should have swam that heat of the medley relay this morning," said Chalmers, who could have had an 11th gold.
"I said I wouldn't do that because I wanted to really prioritise tonight. It's amazing to go past a legend of the sport."
The milestone came as Australia's all-conquering team stormed to a new record tally of golds at a single Games on the final night of the program, roaring past the previous mark of 28 won at Gold Coast 2018.
Queensland speedster Meg Harris became the most successful of all, joining the elite band who've scooped six golds at a single Commonwealth Games as she led another green-and-gold sweep in the 50m freestyle, ahead of Alex Perkins and Shayna Jack, in her farewell race.
Then the 24-year-old, who had powered to victory in 24.23, went on to anchor the women's 4x100 medley relay team, featuring Iona Anderson, Sienna Toohey and Perkins - who ended up with five golds and a silver - to the penultimate win of the week.
Kai Taylor, son of former teen phenomenon Hayley Lewis, was cheered on by his mum while earning a shock 200m freestyle gold.
Brittany Castelluzzo won the 200m fly ahead of bronze medallist Lizzy Dekkers, while Sam Short took the 1500m freestyle for a distance treble as compatriot Ben Goedemans claimed bronze.
Lakeisha Patterson continued the Dolphins' para domination too as she struck 100m free S9 gold ahead of Emily Beecroft.
Fittingly, the last title of the week went to the Dolphins as the men's 4x100 relay quartet of Henry Allan, Sam Williamson, Matt Temple and Flynn Southam landed Australia's eighth gold of the night.
Meanwhile, the Australian women's 3x3 basketball team claimed gold with a 21-11 win over Uganda in the final, as the men's team took silver after a 19-17 loss to England in the final.
The Australian men's wheelchair 3x3 successfully defended their Commonwealth Games title, pulling clear of England 19-13, while the wheelchair women's team won bronze with their 19-17 win over Canada.
Australian weightlifter Eileen Cikamatana was a class above in the women's 86kg event, nailing a 108kg snatch and a 140kg clean and jerk for a Games record total of 248kg.
She is the third female weightlifter in history to achieve the Commonwealth Games feat of three titles in a row, joining India's Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg) and Canadian weightlifter Maude Charron (63kg) after they also won gold in Glasgow.
Cikamatana won her first gold medal with Fiji, before changing allegiance to Australia for the 2022 Games in Birmingham.
Ollie Saxton won bronze in the men's 94kg event earlier in the day.
After six days of competition, Australia stands well clear on the medal tally, with 47 gold, 21 silver and 35 bronze for a total of 103 medals.
Catch up on all the action from day six of the Games in our blog below.
AAP/ABC

You would have assumed he might have been in one of the middle lanes, which are reserved for the fastest qualifiers.
But no.
He was in lane one and led the charge the entire race.

Chad le Clos surpasses Emma McKeon's Games record
South African Chad le Clos has officially become the most decorated athlete in history at the Commonwealth Games.
By winning bronze alongside Pieter Coetzé, Michael Houlie and Ruard van Henen in the men's 4x100m medley relay, he claimed his 21st Commonwealth medal.
That saw him surpass the 20 medal total put up by our Aussie swimming legend Emma McKeon.
His medal tally now includes seven gold, five silver and nine bronze medals, across five editions of the Games: Delhi 2010, Glasgow 2014, Gold Coast 2018, Birmingham 2022 and Glasgow 2026.

Medal tally update: We're on top of the world (okay, Commonwealth)
There's no stopping us now.
Of the 103 total medals won by Australia, 76 of those came from the swimming.
With the swimming wrapped up now at this Commonwealth Games, the Dolphins have made history in the pool, with 37 gold medals.
That has smashed the record of 28 set at the Gold Coast in 2018, and 10 more than Australia won at Birmingham in 2022.

Netball: Diamonds survive scare
The Diamonds remain unbeaten in Glasgow, but they were given a stern test by South Africa in the second half.
The reigning champions won 57-47.
South Africa outscored the Diamonds in the final two quarters, 26-25.
A dominant second term set up the Australian victory, with the Diamonds scoring 18-8 to hold a 32-21 advantage at half-time.
Sophie Garbin was the Diamonds' top scorer for the game with 33 goals.
Kiera Austin added 15.
Elmeré van der Berg scored 39 goals for the South Africans.
The Diamonds, who now have a 4-0 win-loss record, play Northern Ireland in their next pool game at 1am AEST tomorrow.
South Africa meets England.

Australian Cara Feain-Ryan finished one spot outside the medals in the women's 3,000m steeplechase.
Feain-Ryan clocked 9:22.07 to place fourth, with Kenya's world champion Faith Cherotich winning gold in a Games record 9:01.76.
In other track and field results on day six, India's Dilip Gavit won the men's 100m T47 final in 10.71, which was a Games record.
Australia's Jaydon Page (10.97) was fourth.
Canada's Sarah Mitton triumphed in the women's shot put with a winning effort of 19.88m.
Marley Raikiwasa of Australia was sixth with 16.13m.
Aled Davies (F42) of Wales won the men's discus F42-44/F61-64 final with 48.38m.
Australia's Michal Burian (F44) was eighth via a season best of 44.24m.
